In Congress, Elaine uses her experience in the Navy and as a small-business owner to protect our country and create an economy that works for everyone. To help the families, seniors, and businesses of Coastal Virginia, we need leaders with real-world experience. We need leaders who know what it means to serve, have overcome obstacles, and become stronger because of it.
## Priorities
As your Congresswoman, I’ve fought to help businesses, both big and small, across Coastal Virginia create the well-paying jobs with good benefits to ensure our economy thrives and opportunities are available to everyone who works hard.

pages.title: Priorities - Elaine for Congress
pages.text:
## Priorities
There is no greater priority than fighting for those who fought for us.
As a 20-year Navy veteran, I know firsthand the unique challenges and opportunities that our veterans face as they transition out of service.
As a member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, I wrote and passed legislation that provided a critical pay raise for disabled veterans, pressed the VA to find ways to make jobs programs easier to use, cosponsored legislation to increase veteran access to employment programs, and cosponsored a bipartisan bill to allow veterans access to in-state tuition in any state they choose.
And as a veteran, I was appalled by the mistake in the 2017 Tax Bill that was causing some Gold Star families to pay thousands of dollars in additional taxes on their survivor benefits. So, I worked with Republicans and Democrats to ensure those families received every cent they deserve.
Everyone deserves access to quality and affordable health care.
We still have work to do to ensure every American has access to the quality and affordable health care they deserve. That’s why during my time in Congress I’ve fought against efforts to take health care away from Americans and their families. I have, and will continue to, stand up to the pharmaceutical lobby and work to lower prescription drug prices by making less expensive, generic drugs more quickly available to consumers, and require that health insurance providers cover patients with pre-existing conditions.
I will continue to work to improve health care access and affordability and strengthen the ACA to ensure all Americans have access to affordable health coverage.
As your Congresswoman, I’ve fought to help businesses, both big and small, across Coastal Virginia create the well-paying jobs with good benefits to ensure our economy thrives and opportunities are available to everyone who works hard.
Since taking office, I have toured more than 50 local businesses in our district to hear directly from constituents about how Congress can cut through red tape, grow our regional economy, create jobs, and protect the middle class.
I voted to increase the federal minimum wage which could give over 100,000 workers in our district the pay-raise they deserve, and I cosponsored the Paycheck Fairness Act because it is time women receive equal pay for equal work.
As a small business owner, I know the struggles our business community faces and understand the challenges a company can face navigating the red tape in Washington. That’s why I have worked within the community to advocate for small businesses. When I meet with business leaders, I frequently hear that they have well-paying jobs that they cannot fill because they cannot find enough people with the relevant skillset. That is why I am working to support apprenticeship programs, career and technical education, and access to broadband so workers can attain the skills they need to advance their careers.
And as a veteran, I was appalled by the mistake in the 2017 Tax Bill that was causing some Gold Star families to pay thousands of dollars in additional taxes on their survivor benefits. So, I introduced legislation with bipartisan support to ensure those families received every cent they deserve.
Clean air and water isn’t just vital to our way of life in Coastal Virginia, it’s a right.
I am fighting to ensure all Americans breathe clean air and water and have access to pristine natural environments. Coastal Virginia, home to Chesapeake Bay, generates $33 billion for our economy and is one of our nation’s natural treasures.
I’ve fought to ensure the cleanup efforts in The Bay continue to be fully funded to protect our economy and way of life. That’s why I introduced bipartisan legislation to secure $85 billion to advance our shared goals of a clean and healthy Bay.
I am also helping lead the critical fight against drilling off the coast of Virginia. Offshore drilling threatens our national security and safety of our sailors and our tourism economy by spoiling our beautiful beaches and shorelines. I was proud to cosponsor bipartisan legislation to protect our precious coastline.
It is critical to ensure the brave women and men who serve have the resources, support, and equipment they need. That’s why I fought to ensure that our troops received a 3.1% pay raise. As a 20-year Navy veteran, member of the House Armed Services Committee, and Vice Chair of the Seapower and Projection Forces subcommittee, I know the challenges facing our men and women in uniform as they fight for freedom around the globe.
As a 20-year Navy veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know the challenges facing our men and women in uniform as they fight for freedom around the globe. I am committed to supporting policies that will improve life for active duty military, support military families, and ensure the Department of Defense spends your tax dollars as efficiently and effectively as possible.
But a strong, well-funded military is only part of maintaining national security. I support diplomacy to resolve conflicts whenever possible. It is also important to support our allies, such as Israel, to protect U.S. interests around the world.
I am also fighting for Gold Star Families – those who have made the greatest sacrifice imaginable by losing an immediate relative in combat or to a service connected disability.
Every Senior that paid into Social Security and Medicare deserves the benefits they’ve earned.
One of my top priorities is working to strengthen Medicare and Social Security. Hardworking seniors who paid into Social Security and Medicare deserve retirement security and health care coverage.
I’ve sponsored legislation to allow the government to negotiate with drug companies to keep our costs in check while providing seniors with the life-saving medicines they need.
While Washington continues to vote to gut protections for people with pre-existing conditions, I’ve led the fight to protect Virginia’s historic Medicaid expansion. Our focus should be lowering health care costs and the price of prescription drugs – not taking health care away.
Every child deserves access to a world-class education.
Education begins well before K-12 schooling, that’s why as a mother and Congresswoman, I’m proud to support universal pre-K to build a strong foundation for young students to thrive. But this is not only an education issue it is an economic imperative for working and military families.
In Congress, I was proud to support the Rebuild America’s Schools Act that provides direct federal spending for school modernizations, renovations, and repairs, with priority given to public schools in underserved communities. I also advocated for the unique education needs of our military community. I helped secure $50 million to support districts with significant military child enrollment and for military children with severe disabilities.
As your Congresswoman, I’ll continue promoting expansion of career and technical education because while college might not be for everyone, a path to the middle class must be. That’s why I also support adequate student loan forgiveness so students who want to go to college can. No student should be deterred from seeking higher education because of the cost.
Reducing America’s reliance on foreign oil, while simultaneously combatting climate change is essential to our national security and protecting our coastal region. This is a threat Congress must address today, particularly in coastal communities that are impacted by seal level rise and recurrent flooding.
I’ve led the charge to make Coastal Virginia a national and global leader in our clean energy future. For our district this is not a problem of tomorrow, it’s a threat today. I have laid out a bold vision for cutting greenhouse gas emissions while investing in the jobs and infrastructure of the future.
As a nuclear engineer in the Navy, I saw firsthand that nuclear power, when deployed safely and responsibly, can play a key role in our green energy future. That’s why I introduced legislation to encourage innovation in nuclear technologies.
I am also helping lead the critical fight against drilling off the coast of Virginia. Offshore drilling threatens our national security and safety of our sailors and our tourism economy by spoiling our beautiful beaches and shorelines. I was proud to cosponsor bipartisan legislation to protect our precious coastline.
Investing in our nation’s infrastructure is vital to boosting not only our district’s economy, but the global economy.
Our district, which is home to one of the largest ports on the East Coast, depends on improving our maritime infrastructure. That’s why I secured $15 million for operations and maintenance at Norfolk Harbor and led a bipartisan effort urging Congress to fund infrastructure projects in military communities. I am proud to have helped deliver needed funds for resiliency projects for communities battling sea level rise and recurrent flooding
But our needs go beyond maritime infrastructure, roads, and bridges. Investments in broadband infrastructure are necessary to ensure that our rural communities stay connected in the ever-expanding global economy. Critical to those investments is protecting net-neutrality. I’m proud to have sponsored legislation to restore net neutrality so the farmers, entrepreneurs, and innovators of Coastal Virginia can stay competitive.
A woman’s right to choose should be made between a woman, her health care provider, and her faith. We need to enshrine reproductive freedom protections into federal law to protect Americans from government overreach and restore the rights of women across the country. I will continue to be an advocate in Congress for women and fight to protect the rights of all Americans, including the right to choose.
We need commonsense measures to keep our communities safe from gun violence and protect law-abiding citizens’ Second Amendment rights.
As a former Navy Commander and now as a Member of Congress, I took an oath to protect this nation and its people, while simultaneously swearing to protect our Constitution. I believe that law-abiding citizens should be able to own guns and exercise their second amendment rights, but commonsense measures are necessary to keep our communities safe from preventable gun violence.
I joined bipartisan commonsense reform efforts like requiring universal background checks and encouraging red flag laws, which can prevent an individual from purchasing or retaining their firearm for a certain period if they are determined to be a danger to themselves or others.
But this issue took on even greater urgency after the mass shooting in Virginia Beach. Along with all members of the Virginia Beach community, I will forever remember and honor the individuals who were tragically taken from their families and loved ones.

pages.title: Priorities - Elaine for Congress
pages.text:
## The Experience to Get Things Done
I raised my right hand at 17 years old and joined the Navy, spending the next 20 years of my life on combatant ships, deploying six times to the Middle East and Western Pacific, and conducting operations on destroyers, cruisers, and aircraft carriers. In the Navy, I learned about the importance of serving others and putting their needs above myself.
When I retired from the Navy, I began a small business from a block of clay on my kitchen table and grew the Mermaid Factory into a thriving family business in Hampton Roads that created jobs and gave back to our community.
I used my experience in the military and as a small business owner to run for Congress where I advocated and delivered for the working families of Hampton Roads. From the largest expansion of veterans benefits in our lifetimes to cutting prescription drug costs, I fought for and passed legislation in Congress that has had a real impact on the lives of people who put their trust in me. But I also saw how broken Congress can be, especially when it is used as a tool by corrupt politicians like Jen Kiggans to benefit her dark money donors and further her own political interests.
Putting an end to this culture of corruption starts with two major changes : ending the influence special interests have on our political system, and stopping the bad policies that drive up our costs.
Protect Hampton Roads and the Chesapeake Bay
Hampton Roads often feels the impacts of climate change before anywhere else in the Commonwealth or country.
In Congress, I secured funding to mitigate the impacts of sea-level rise, supported legislation to invest in climate resilient infrastructure, and founded the bipartisan Offshore Wind Caucus. I have also been a strong advocate for the Chesapeake Bay, leading the effort to fully fund the EPA’s Chesapeake Bay Program at $85 million — ensuring a clean and healthy Bay for our communities, our economy, and our way of life.
I will continue to lead efforts to combat climate change’s impact on our local community, fight against offshore drilling, restore the Chesapeake Bay, and ensure Hampton Roads has clean air and water.
Protect Our Seniors
Seniors who worked hard their entire lives and paid into Social Security and Medicare deserve to be secure in retirement with the peace of mind that their benefits will be there when they need them—without cuts.
Kiggans’ decisive vote for the One Big Beautiful Bill enacted the largest SNAP cut in the program’s history, threatening to take away food assistance for more than 22,000 households in VA-02, including seniors.
The legislation introduces stricter Medicaid eligibility checks, imposes work verification requirements for near-elderly adults, and weakens nursing home staffing standards. It also allows expanded Affordable Care Act (ACA) premium subsidies to expire
We must honor our commitments to our seniors and retirees. I will continue to advocate for strengthening Medicare and Social Security, stand firm against any efforts to gut seniors’ hard-earned benefits, and oppose cuts to these critical programs.
Strengthen our National Security and Care for our Military Families
As a 20-year Navy veteran, I know how important it is to protect the homeland and ensure that our men and women in uniform have the resources and equipment they need to fight for and defend our freedoms.
I used my experience in the Navy to champion legislation in Congress that provided troops with a pay raise, invested in our warfighters, strengthened naval seapower, and led efforts to deter our enemies like Russia, China, and Iran.
The war in Iran is another unnecessary and endless military intervention in the Middle East that is putting a strain on working families in Hampton Roads, and costing precious American lives and resources that should be spent here at home. Moreover, the war has left Americans no safer, and has emboldened Iran and done nothing to contain Iran’s nuclear ambitions or support for terrorist proxies.
I also know that a strong border is essential to strengthening our nation’s security, and I was proud to support comprehensive efforts in Congress to deter illegal immigration and strengthen border security, while also providing a pathway to citizenship for those who follow our nation’s laws.
I will continue to fight to improve the quality of life for active duty military personnel and their families, ensure they have the resources they need to deter our adversaries and keep us safe, serve as a check against reckless foreign wars that put our servicemembers at risk, and cost American taxpayers, and strengthen our bord er security.
Honor America’s Promise to our Veterans
As a 20-year Navy veteran, I know firsthand the unique challenges that our veterans face as they transition out of service. There is nothing greater than fighting for and improving the lives of military families and veterans.
In Congress, I served on the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee and was instrumental in passing the PACT Act–the largest expansion of veterans’ benefits in our lifetime. I also introduced and passed the Gold Star Families Act to provide tax relief for Gold Star families and championed legislation to provide three cost of living increases to veterans.
I also pressed the Department of Veterans Affairs to find ways to make veterans jobs programs easier to use, cosponsored legislation to increase veteran access to employment programs, and cosponsored a bipartisan bill to increase education opportunities.
Kiggans was a major proponent of DOGE, calling it “so necessary” as the agency she backed caused “the termination of more than $8.3 million in grants,” many of which directly impacted military families and veterans throughout Hampton Roads.
In Congress, I will continue to fight for my fellow veterans to reverse the devastating DOGE cuts endorsed by Jen Kiggans that have gutted veterans’ care, work to cut red tape in the VA system, and ensure that our veterans get the care they need and deserve.
Oppose Endless Wars that Raise Gas Prices and the Tariffs on Our Allies that Raise Costs on Americans
Gas prices and the cost of everyday items are spiking to levels that have left middle class families struggling to fill their tanks and feed their families because of Jen Kiggans’ lockstep support for Donald Trump’s agenda. She has voted 100% of the time with Donald Trump, including for his reckless tariffs and foreign policy.
In Congress, I will serve as a check on Trump’s bad decisions that are costing our families, fight to repeal the tariffs, and reverse legislation and policy decisions that have increased energy costs.
Make Life More Affordable
Throughout Hampton Roads, I hear the same story from Virginians and their families: “We’re working harder than ever, but we can barely keep up.” From gas and grocery prices to prescription drug costs, housing, and childcare, the rising cost of living continue to squeeze Virginians.
We can’t expect families to get ahead when they are barely getting by. Making life more affordable for Virginians means taking on Jen Kiggans’ and Donald Trump’s failed policies that have cost the average American household $1,700 more over the last year alone.
I will address the cost of living crisis that Kiggans unleashed and lower prices for working families.
Virginians Want More Affordability and Less Corruption.
In the Navy, when the mission isn’t going according to plan, you right the ship. That is what we need to do now more than ever in Washington.
I am running for Congress because I have fought for our country before, and I am ready to fight for it again.
My Plan to Right the Ship:
- Ban Members of Congress and their Families from Trading Stocks While in Office – Serving the American people is about putting others above oneself. No one should profit off of holding office–especially members of Congress who write our nation’s laws, regulate industry, and receive classified briefings that members of the public cannot access. I support banning members of Congress and their families from trading individual stocks while holding office.
- End the Blatant Prediction Market Insider Trading – Members of Congress, congressional staff, executive branch employees, and political appointees should not use nonpublic information to buy, sell, or exchange prediction market contracts related to political outcomes or government policy. Public servants should never make money on the policies and decisions they help make and shape–especially those with access to classified or national security information. It’s unfair, and it’s wrong. Public service is about putting the American people first, not using insider information to enrich yourself.
- If a Politician Steals from Taxpayers, they face Mandatory Jail Time – The American people who work hard and pay their taxes should know that members of Congress are being good stewards of their taxes. Stealing from taxpayers is an egregious breach of trust and there’s no room in Congress for members who abuse their office. I believe that members who steal taxpayer funds, including blatant tax evasion, should serve mandatory jail time and be expelled from Congress. No questions asked.
- Reform Campaign Finance Laws and Get Dark Money out of Politics – The Citizens United decision has allowed dark money, special interests, and the ultra-wealthy to corrode and abuse our political system and democracy. Congress must pass a law to significantly reduce the influence that dark money and special interests have on our elections and in our system. I was proud to support legislation that overturns the disastrous Citizens United decision when in Congress, and I will continue to fight for the For the People Act to restore fairness and power back to the people.
- End the Broken Pardon System to Ensure Equal Justice for All – Politicians from both parties have abused the pardon system to reward their families and wealthy and well-connected donors with political favors. It’s true when then President Joe Biden pardoned his son Hunter and it’s true when President Trump pardoned a Chinese cryptocurrency billionaire who was in prison for enabling money laundering. That’s unacceptable, and we must reform the current system so that those with money and connections don’t get special treatment.
We need Congress to work for the working people of this country, not just Donald Trump’s friends and Kiggans’ ultra-wealthy donors. That’s why we must put an end to this corruption agenda that is leaving Virginians behind and driving up costs. Their policies are squeezing working families and raising the cost of living on everything from gas, groceries, and health care costs. Virginians deserve better.
My Plan to Make Health Care Affordable & Accessible for Every Virginian
Every Virginian deserves access to affordable, high-quality health care, regardless of their income or where they live. Jen Kiggans disagrees. Despite being a former Navy pilot and a nurse, Kiggans has voted time and time again to rip health care away from her fellow veterans and raise the cost of health care for middle-class families in order to give tax cuts to billionaires.
I have a different definition of public service. From lowering ACA premiums, to taking on Big Pharma to cut prescription drug costs, to cutting seniors’ out-of-pocket drug costs and capping insulin at $35 a month, I have a record of delivering affordable and accessible health care for every member of her community. Now I am running to cut the cost of care, cut the complexity of care, and close the rural health care gap, so no Virginian has to pay too much, spend too much time, or travel too far just to get the care they need.
Cut the Cost of Care
- Cut health care costs for the middle class by restoring ACA premium subsidies.
- Cut health care costs for seniors by expanding the number of drugs Medicare can negotiate on and extending the reduced cost benefits to people on private insurance.
- Cut health care costs for working families by cracking down on predatory medical debt collectors, pharmaceutical monopolies, and Wall Street firms buying up hospitals for profit.
Cut the Complexity of Care
- Cut the complexity of care for military families by allowing military children to stay on their parents’ Tricare Plan until age 26.
- Cut the complexity of care for patients and providers by standardizing insurance paperwork and billing requirements, and modernizing the Prior Authorization process.
- Help rural hospitals stay open by restoring the $1 trillion Jen Kiggans and Donald Trump cut from Medicaid in order to give tax cuts to billionaires.
- Ensure equal health care access for rural Virginians by expanding federal loan repayment for doctors and nurses who commit to serving at least five years in rural communities.
- Expand access to telehealth, mobile health clinics, community health centers, and rural emergency medical services so geography isn’t a barrier to care.
